raw_response:
I have 200 mu, so I cannot manage it like a tiny household plot, but I still do not farm by theory alone. I have been on this land 40 years, and what stays in my head is what works in Quzhou under our water and our prices. This year I will keep the main income on the wheat-maize rotation because it is stable and I have well irrigation, then keep some millet because it is more drought-tolerant and cheaper to manage, and keep squash on a smaller block because it can bring cash if the market is decent, though it needs more labor and more attention. I will not spread money blindly at the start. Wheat already in the field gets priority now for water and topdressing, because if I miss that timing I cannot recover yield later. For the spring crops, I will plant enough to diversify, but not so much squash that I get trapped by labor and market risk. On 200 mu I can hire machinery and a few hands when needed, so I will use round, workable rates, split nitrogen on the main crops, and keep irrigation to the stages that matter most.
